2608.25382.title: Q&A or Document-Based? The Effects of Interface Type on How Screen Reader Users Access Interconnected Documents
2608.25382.paper_summary: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users are increasingly engaging with large language model (LLM) interfaces to access documents, but it is unclear how such systems support or hinder their ability to build interconnected knowledge. To examine this gap, we compared a Question-Answer Interface (QAI) that supports open-ended conversational inquiry, with a Document Interface (DI) based mostly on traditional structured text document navigation. We recruited 16 BLV screen reader users where they used both interfaces to explore two fictional worlds. Data from interaction logs, concept maps, decision-based tasks, and semi-structured interviews provide comparative insights into how interface design supports knowledge construction. Findings show that participants visited more distinct documents with the DI and formed larger and more correct mental models with the DI than with the QAI. They were also more able to apply knowledge they had gained. Simultaneously, many still preferred the QAI and often estimated that they had explored more, formed better mental models and applied their models better when acquiring the information with the QAI, despite this not being the case. Our analysis suggests possible interface design reasons for these differences and highlights some of the risks introduced by using question-answer interfaces to access information spaces.
2608.25382.paper_summary_zh: 盲人和低視力（BLV）使用者越來越多地使用大型語言模型（LLM）介面來訪問文件，但尚不清楚這些系統如何支持或妨礙他們建立互聯知識的能力。<lb/>為了檢視這一差距，我們比較了一個支持開放式對話詢問的問題回答介面（QAI）與一個主要基於傳統結構化文本文件導航的文件介面（DI）。<lb/>我們招募了16名BLV螢幕閱讀器使用者，讓他們使用這兩種介面探索兩個虛構世界。<lb/>來自互動日誌、概念圖、基於決策的任務和半結構化訪談的數據提供了有關介面設計如何支持知識建構的比較見解。<lb/>研究結果顯示，參與者在使用DI時訪問了更多不同的文件，並且在DI中形成的心理模型比在QAI中更大且更正確。<lb/>他們也更能應用所獲得的知識。<lb/>同時，許多人仍然偏好QAI，並且經常估計他們在使用QAI獲取信息時探索了更多、形成了更好的心理模型並且更好地應用了這些模型，儘管事實並非如此。<lb/>我們的分析提出了這些差異的可能介面設計原因，並突顯了使用問題回答介面訪問信息空間所引入的一些風險。
